feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
entry.summary: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

entry.title: Texas leaders point to 'birth tourism' as Trump opposes birthright citizenship
entry.summary: Texas officials have tried to take action to punish clinics encouraging "birth tourism." But there are laws that can be used there, if there's evidence and they're enforced.

entry.title: Scientists find evidence of ancient drug use in prehistoric teeth
entry.summary: A new study on ancient human remains finds evidence for the habitual use of betel nuts, dating back to the Ice Age. The finding offers some of the oldest archaeological evidence of psychoactive drug use, and potential insights into how use of betel nuts, now popular for their stimulant effects, evolved.

entry.title: People living in bombed-out buildings in Gaza at risk from collapse
entry.summary: A bombed-out building in Gaza sheltering around 100 people collapsed, and there are hundreds more like it that could, too

entry.title: Ed Sheeran tour continues to attract controversy following Macklemore's removal
entry.summary: The saga of Ed Sheeran and Macklemore continues, which began with a political statement on stage, now involves billionaire sports team owners, musicians quitting a tour and millions in donations.

entry.title: This week in science: T. rex footprints, solar 'superflares,' and benefits of reading
entry.summary: Paleontologists have discovered the tracks of a giant — the fossilized footprints of T. rex. Plus, solar "superflares" and the brain benefits of reading in this week's Short Wave science news roundup.

entry.title: Fears grow that Trump could use military to influence the upcoming election
entry.summary: There is growing concern that President Trump may deploy U.S. military to polling places in the upcoming elections, despite strict state and federal laws against such a move.

entry.title: 'If I Go Will They Miss Me' is an intense but tender coming-of-age story set in L.A.
entry.summary: A 12-year-old idolizes his father who is just home from prison in this intense but tender drama from writer-director Walter Thompson-Hernandez.

entry.title: With AI, what's more important for the U.S. — winning or safety?
entry.summary: Everyone is talking about the spectre of AI catastrophe. Can the U.S. and China agree on guardrails to blunt the biggest risks when their leaders meet next week?

entry.title: Trump threatens to tear down the Kennedy Center, as legal battle continues
entry.summary: The president made the remark to reporters amidst back-and-forth developments in federal court, including an allegation that a forklift repeatedly struck the center.
